newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nearly 80 pct of Taiwan firms in black Jan-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 80 pct of Taiwan firms in black Jan-Sept.

text.p: Nearly 80 percent of 339 Taiwanese listed firms that reported results in the first nine months of 1996 were profitable, a poor performance compared to 1995, the Economic Daily News said on Saturday.
As of November 1, 339 of a total 367 listed companies in Taiwan had announced their January-September results.

Of the 339 firms, 270 or 79.65 percent had reported profits, with the remaining 69 firms or 20.35 percent reporting losses, said the paper, which based the findings on its own calculations according to results released by each firm.

It said the relatively large number of companies suffering losses during the period reflected faltering export growth which the paper linked to an escalation in tensions between Taiwan and China since mid-1995.
"This (the results) indicated stagnant export growth since communist China's military threats in the latter half of 1995," the paper said.
The mid- and downstream industry of the electronics, textiles and plastics outperformed other industries, it said.
Only 15 firms had reported earnings per share (EPS) of more than T$3 in the period, it said.
The top three earners were Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co Ltd with an EPS of T$6.04, Asia Polymer Corp with T$4.9 and Synnex Technology International Corp with T$3.96, the paper said.
China held war games in July and August 1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui launched a landmark private visit to the United States.
China held further military drills in the Taiwan Strait, which separates the island from mainland China, around the time of Taiwan's first direct presidential elections on March 23.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, said the exercises were to deter any Taiwanese voters who wanted independence. Taipei denies it wants independence. -Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
